picks.title: Google turns on PMax image extraction by default from December 4
picks.rationale: Starting December 4, Google AI will pull images from advertisers' landing pages into Performance Max creative by default. Advertisers and API tool builders have to opt out before then if they want to keep control of their visuals.
picks.excerpt: From December 4, Google AI will scan landing pages for images to enrich Performance Max creative by default; advertisers and API tools must actively opt out.

picks.title: Walmart Embraces AI Agents That Shop on Behalf of Customers
picks.rationale: Walmart is publishing rules for third-party AI shopping agents, including spending controls and transaction approvals, while Amazon blocks them. The largest US retailers are now split on whether to open agentic checkout.
picks.excerpt: Walmart is setting the rules AI shopping agents must follow to buy on its site on customers' behalf, with spending controls and transaction approvals, while Amazon blocks such agents.

picks.title: ChatGPT Ads Is Expanding To New Markets And Exploring New Ad Formats
picks.rationale: ChatGPT Ads is opening in 26 more countries after passing 100,000 advertisers. That widens the in-assistant ad surface for international media plans.
picks.excerpt: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries after more than 100,000 advertisers used the platform, while OpenAI is still working out what conversational ad formats will look like.

picks.title: Yelp charges $30 a month for AI agent that answers and qualifies leads
picks.rationale: Yelp launched Smart Lead Reply, a paid AI agent that answers and qualifies quote requests for $30 a month. It is a priced, concrete AI lead-generation product for local service businesses.
picks.excerpt: Yelp's Smart Lead Reply AI agent answers and qualifies Request a Quote leads for movers, roofers and plumbers for $30 a month, plus AI calls to restaurants.

picks.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity
picks.rationale: On its Q3 call, Meta said its Muse AI app has passed 10M users and that shopping is one of its top uses. That makes Muse a sizable new AI product-discovery surface that brands and Meta's ad business will target.
picks.excerpt: Meta told investors on its Q3 call that its Muse AI app passed 10M users, with shopping among the top uses, signaling a new AI-mediated discovery surface for brands.

https://www.adexchanger.com/marketers/ch.new_action: New announcement: ChatGPT Ads is expanding to 26 additional countries and has passed 100,000 advertisers. The 10-17 card covered measurement and visual formats, and the 10-21 card covered auto-enabled creative enhancements. Neither covered the market expansion.

dedup.note: Pool: 12 items. Dropped (1) Marketing Dive Dollar Shave Club: enrichment rejected it in the 10-21 swap pass because AI was incidental to the campaign concept, and we did not reconsider. (2) AdExchanger 'Inside the Stack' Amazon Ads: a vendor-exec interview and advertorial, also rejected on 10-21. It is also close to the 10-19 Amazon Full-Funnel AI card. (3) SEJ 'AI search tools cited a made-up concept': GEO/SEO research with no paid surface, rejected on 10-21. (4) OpenAI 'building ChatGPT ad stack': an engineering explainer in the same ChatGPT Ads cluster as the AdExchanger expansion pick. We kept only one ChatGPT Ads story, and this one has no og:image. (5) Modern Retail Target holiday push: AI is one of three elements and the headline stands without it, so it fails the delete-AI test. It is also close to running holiday and AI-assistant coverage. (6) PPC Land Meta/Nest case study: a vendor case study with no baseline, and it would have been a third PPC Land pick. (7) SEJ China GEO rulebook: commentary on voluntary GEO standards that is mostly SEO-side. Checks: Walmart's history_match (the 10-12 MK Naver/Amazon lockout card) is a different retailer and a different action, so the verdict is new. PMax's history_match (the 10-16 Meta product browsing card) is a different platform and feature, so the verdict is new. Muse 10M is a new Q3 earnings disclosure, distinct from the 10-11 HUMAN 72% and 10-12 Muse ad-account cards. Outlets: PPC Land x2, Adweek, AdExchanger, TechCrunch (4 distinct, max 2).
